requirement_text.REQ-039: GitHub issue #71. Companion (+1) registration through a companion code, with consent before storage and invited_by_user_id attribution. Implements USER-STORIES B8 / STORY-DETAILS B8 (Bring someone with me), the +1 half of PRD FR-5, sequenced after REQ-038 (Depends on B7). A host holding a companion code (invite_codes.grants_companion_of = host user id, issued by REQ-037) forwards the link; the guest redeems through REQ-038's validation table unchanged, no parallel implementation. A code with grants_companion_of = X sets registrations.invited_by_user_id = X (PRD FR-5, DESIGN-REVIEW F10 -- one field is both the +1 mechanic and referral reporting, no second column/table; invited_by_user_id already exists in schema.ts, no migration). The companion completes NAME, PHONE, COMPANY only (not the full REQ-019 form) -- the same reduced set REQ-030's walk-in flow uses; the design states whether REQ-030's collection path is reused or why not. Phone is required here even though PRD 5 marks it optional generally, mirroring REQ-030's own door-minimum reasoning. Consent before storage is the security-critical property: nothing (no User row carrying their name, no Profile row, no invited_by relationship, no partial-form draft) is written before consent_pd_at is set; this differs from REQ-019's resumable partial-write pattern (consent already established before the first partial write there) -- here consent comes first in the flow and there is no legitimate pre-consent write at all, stated explicitly so an implementer does not reach for REQ-019's write-as-you-go pattern by analogy. Companions occupy a normal seat -- a full event waitlists them like anyone else, no reserved-seat mechanic. One use unless the organizer said otherwise is just max_uses on REQ-033's row, defaulting to 1 at REQ-037's issue time -- REQ-038's existing spent-code refusal covers reuse, no second check. Both are told: the guest gets their own admission result, the host is told their guest is coming, both transactional through REQ-025's ledger; the host notification carries the guest's name and company only (S3 -- the host is not an organizer). The guest arrives via /start's existing REQ-014 first-contact path and REQ-019's consent gate, not a bypass around them.

task.description: WF-02 Step 1 (Design) for REQ-039, on branch feature/WF02-REQ-039 (verified branch matches, commit c65525b at run start; working tree clean before and after). Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md mapping all 9 acceptance criteria to concrete design elements. Re-verified directly against the live apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (lines 272-274) that registrations.invited_by_user_id already exists as a nullable uuid FK to users.id, onDelete restrict -- zero schema change anywhere in this design, DATA-DESIGNER NOT dispatched. Read the actual REQ-038-merged code (domain/inviteCode.ts's redeemInviteCode/validateInviteCodeForRedemption), REQ-030's walkin.ts message-carrier pattern, and handlers/start.ts's REQ-038 consent-gated deep-link resolution before designing, per the dispatch prompt. All 6 design questions resolved explicitly: (1) collection-before-consent reuses REQ-030's message-text-carrier pattern (one guest-typed 'Name | Company | Phone' reply, re-parsed from the confirm message's own text on the final tap) rather than any DB draft row, with an explicit section (design doc section 3.3) stating WHY REQ-019's write-as-you-go pattern is not reused even though consent_pd_at is already true by the time collection starts -- the reasoning is 'no half-registered stranger' plus 'one atomic unit matching AC1's shape', not just chronology. (2) The companion-vs-personal/bulk distinction point is handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink, inserted between the existing hasConsented check and the existing unconditional redeemInviteCode call, using the same getInviteCodeByCode read redeemInviteCode itself already performs (design doc section 2). (3) Host notification is a new NotificationKind 'companion_registered', sent via the existing sendLedgeredNotification (idempotent on (registrationId, kind)), modeled on organizerRequests.ts's sendApprovalNotification -- its composeMessage closure structurally never reads profiles.phone/email, satisfying S3/S11 by construction, not by a runtime filter (design doc section 6). (4) invited_by_user_id already exists -- confirmed by direct schema read, zero migration. (5) Capacity/waitlist is confirmed unchanged: decideRegistrationOutcome is called with the identical seatsLeft/inviteSatisfied:true shape for every code kind, no new branch. (6) One-use enforcement is confirmed as entirely validateInviteCodeForRedemption's existing usedCount>=maxUses row -- no second check anywhere. The extension to redeemInviteCode itself (design doc section 5) is a minimal, backward-compatible delta: one new optional parameter (companionProfile, defaulting to null for every existing caller), grantsCompanionOf added to the already-existing locked codeRows SELECT, invitedByUserId set on the existing insert/update from that field (a no-op for personal/bulk codes since they always have grantsCompanionOf=null), and a reuse (not a new function) of domain/profile.ts's existing createWalkinProfile for the Profile insert when companionProfile is supplied.
acceptance_criteria: A guest redeeming a companion code whose grants_companion_of is host H gets a registration with invited_by_user_id = H's user id and invite_code_id set to that code -- verified by reading the row.
git grep over apps/bot finds no companion-specific column, no referral table and no second attribution field: invited_by_user_id is the only mechanism, and no migration adds another.

Abandoning the companion flow AT OR BEFORE the consent step leaves ZERO new users rows, ZERO new profiles rows and ZERO new registrations rows for that guest -- run against a guest the bot has never seen; a run that reaches consent before abandoning is not evidence.
Completing the flow collects name, phone and company and nothing further -- no experience-level, student-flag or links question is asked.
A companion redeeming against a FULL event is waitlisted, not admitted, and not given a seat outside capacity.
A second person attempting to redeem a single-use companion code is refused and no registration is created, verified by constructing max_uses=1, redeeming once, then attempting again.

Both the guest and the host receive exactly one message on a successful companion registration; the host's message contains the guest's name and company and contains NEITHER the guest's phone NOR their email.
The guest's phone appears in NO log line and in NO audit_log payload.
Each companion registration writes exactly one audit_log row, counted before and after.

result.summary: Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md (8 sections plus open questions and a types-only component/type structure section, full AC map in section 7). Confirmed directly against the live apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts that registrations.invited_by_user_id already exists (nullable uuid FK, onDelete restrict) -- zero schema change, no new column/table/migration anywhere in this design. DATA-DESIGNER is NOT dispatched for this run. All 6 design questions from the dispatch prompt are resolved explicitly with stated reasoning (see task.description above); in particular the consent-before-storage mechanism (question 1) is resolved as REQ-030's message-carrier pattern reused (not REQ-019's write-as-you-go), with an explicit 'why not REQ-019 by analogy' subsection (design doc section 3.3) covering both the chronological point and the deeper reason (no half-registered stranger; one atomic unit). Design gate reviewers should check in particular: (a) section 3.1's step-by-step ordering table against AC3's exact wording -- the pre-existing bare users-row-from-resolveOrCreateUser exception is named explicitly and reasoned as pre-existing, unmodified platform behavior, not a new write this requirement introduces; (b) section 5's redeemInviteCode extension -- confirm it is genuinely a backward-compatible delta (new optional parameter defaulting to null, one added SELECT column, one added insert/update field, one reused existing function call) and not a parallel/forked implementation; (c) section 6's host-notification S3/S11 reasoning -- confirm the composeMessage closure is described as structurally never reading phone/email, not merely filtering it at render time; (d) that no implementation code appears anywhere -- every new function in the closing 'Component/type structure' section is a bare type/interface/signature declaration, no bodies, matching REQ-033/037/038's own artefact style; (e) the open questions section's item 1 (an already-profiled returning guest hitting profiles_user_id_unique) -- confirm this is a genuine, correctly-identified gap rather than something the design should have resolved.
issues: OPEN (design doc, Open Questions #1): a companion guest who already has a Profile row (returning bot user, already onboarded via REQ-019, redeeming a companion code for a different event) would violate profiles_user_id_unique if createWalkinProfile's plain INSERT is reused as-is. Two directions are equally defensible (skip the reduced-field conversation and redeem immediately vs. still collect fields and UPDATE instead of INSERT) and neither is chosen here -- must be resolved before BACKEND-DEV can implement design doc section 5 point 4 for this branch.

OPEN (design doc, Open Questions #3): exact file placement for the new parse/format/confirm functions (domain/walkin.ts, co-located with the REQ-030 pattern they mirror, vs. domain/inviteCode.ts, co-located with the feature they serve) -- either is structurally correct, left for BACKEND-DEV.

OPEN (design doc, Open Questions #4): exact callback_data string/prefix for the confirm button and all new catalog copy (field-collection prompt, confirm message trailing text, host notification text) are naming/wiring/content details with no behavioral consequence -- not invented here, left for BACKEND-DEV/CONTENT-BA, same precedent prior invite-code requirements' artefacts already established for provisional copy.

OPEN (design doc, Open Questions #5): whether the companion's field-collection prompt states the event title/host name could not be checked against USER-STORIES B8's verbatim 'Conversation' text -- that source document is not present in this repository. The design assumes yes (an Event: line, mirroring formatWalkinConfirmMessage) but does not specify exact copy.
